function.name: user_authentication_login
function.description: Authenticate a user by their username and password, providing a token for successful authentication. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

username.description: The username of the user attempting to log in.

password.description: The password for the specified username.

remember_me.description: Whether to create a persistent session for the user.

login_attempts.description: The number of consecutive failed login attempts for the user. After a certain threshold, additional security checks may be required.

last_login.description: The timestamp of the user's last successful login, in the format of 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS', such as '2023-01-15 13:45:00'.

message.content:
Sure! The `user_authentication_login` function is designed to authenticate a user based on their credentials. Here’s a quick rundown of its parameters:

| Parameter | Type   | Description |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| `username` | `string` | The user’s login name. |
| `password` | `string` | The user’s password. |
| `remember_me` | `boolean` (default: `false`) | If set to `true`, the system will create a persistent session (e.g., “Remember me” functionality). |
| `login_attempts` | `number` (default: `0`) | Tracks how many consecutive failed login attempts have occurred. This can trigger extra security measures if it exceeds a threshold. |
| `last_login` | `string` (default: `null`) | Timestamp of the user’s last successful login, formatted like `'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS'`. |

When you call this function with a username and password, it will return a response indicating whether the login was successful and, if so, provide an authentication token.
